subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — follow-up & sizing for latency SLOs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lewis <jessica.lewis@helixdx.com>; Michael Choi <michael.choi@helixdx.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call highlights / Helix workload notes (from you):
- Use case: real-time chat completions for diagnostics assistant that streams tokens as they’re generated.
- Average reply size: ~200 tokens; typical turn length 150–300 tokens.
- Concurrency target: peak ~150 concurrent active sessions, target 95th pct workload sizing at 200 to include buffer.
- Latency SLOs: target p95 end-to-end response latency <= 150ms today; Helix mentioned goal to tighten to ~100ms for high-priority flows.
- Streaming requirements: first token should begin to stream within 50ms for interactive feel; subsequent tokens streamed continuously.

What we’ll validate in Dedicated:
1) GPU type comparison: H100 vs A100 80GB vs L40S-style cards (cost/latency tradeoffs).
2) Reserved throughput sizing to meet p95 latency SLO at your concurrency and average tokens/req.
3) Concurrency behavior and streaming latency (first-byte and steady-state).
4) Fallbacks/autoscaling tolerance and plan for canary/rollout.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- We’ll send a recommended sizing matrix (A100/H100/L40S options) and a baseline throughput plan by EOD tomorrow. (Lauren will include per-GPU reserved throughput numbers and expected p95 estimates.)
- Helix to confirm target SLOs to validate for the POC (finalize whether target is p95<=100ms or p95<=150ms).
- If Helix agrees, we’ll schedule a 2-week Dedicated POC with a small reserved commit to validate performance and then scale to production sizing.

Attachments: we’ll share a short sizing spreadsheet and a performance matrix for the three GPU classes.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jessica Lewis <jessica.lewis@helixdx.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Choi <michael.choi@helixdx.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side so your sizing can be as accurate as possible: 

- We want the POC to validate the stricter SLO: p95 <= 100ms for our priority flows (these are the clinician-facing completion requests). For lower-priority background flows we can accept p95 <= 200ms.
- Streaming: we care about first-byte latency specifically — aim for first token <= 50ms for priority flows.
- Concurrency: peak expected is 150 concurrent, but we’d like sizing for 200 to include headroom.
- Model: we plan to run an open model equivalent to a 13B/70B family (quantized), but we’ll confirm exact weights before the POC.

We’re happy to move to a 2-week Dedicated POC. Can you include cost/commit ranges for the different GPU combos in the sizing doc? Also please include whether we can mix GPU types for burst capacity (e.g., reserve A100 and burst to H100) and how routing/fallback would work.

–Jessica
Director, Product (AI) | Helix Diagnostics
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lewis <jessica.lewis@helixdx.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing options (H100 / A100 / L40S) — draft

Jessica — attaching the sizing spreadsheet and a short performance matrix (see attached files). High-level guidance below based on the numbers you provided (avg 200 tokens, concurrency 150–200, streaming first-byte target <=50ms):

Option A — H100 (high-performance, lowest latency):
- Recommended reserved config: 4 x H100 nodes configured for inference (model parallel where needed)
- Reserved throughput: ~12,000 tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Expected p95: ~65–95ms (dependent on model size & quantization)
- First-byte streaming: typically <=40ms for small initial context slices
- Pros: meets sub-100ms p95 with native FP16/AMP paths.
- Cons: highest cost per hour.

Option B — A100 80GB (balanced cost/perf):
- Recommended reserved config: 6 x A100 80GB
- Reserved throughput: ~9,000 tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Expected p95: ~90–140ms
- First-byte streaming: ~45–70ms
- Pros: good balance for larger models and multi-tenancy.
- Cons: may need more nodes to hit strict p95 for 70B-class models.

Option C — L40S / L4-class (cost-optimized inference):
- Recommended reserved config: 8 x L40S-style nodes
- Reserved throughput: ~6,000 tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Expected p95: ~120–220ms
- First-byte streaming: ~60–120ms
- Pros: most cost-efficient for quantized 13B workloads; good for non-priority flows.
- Cons: may not meet your 100ms p95 for priority clinician flows.

Mixing GPU types / burst behavior:
- Yes — Redwood Dedicated supports mixed pools. We can reserve a baseline on A100 (or L40S) and configure a burst pool on H100 that traffic can failover/route to when latency SLOs are at risk. We’ll include routing policy examples in the Drive doc (priority rules, cost caps, and automatic fallback thresholds).

Next recommended action:
1) Confirm you want us to design the POC against the tight p95 <=100ms target for priority flows.
2) If yes, pick 2 candidate configs you want validated (we recommend H100 baseline + A100 baseline as two test points).
3) We’ll schedule a 3-hour baseline benchmark run during the POC kickoff to validate first-byte and p95 numbers using your sample traces.

Attachments: throughput-sizing.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-performance-matrix.pdf

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lewis <jessica.lewis@helixdx.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Next steps & pilot commercial terms — Helix Dedicated POC

Jessica — following Lauren’s sizing options, happy to propose a commercial path for the 2-week Dedicated POC: 

Pilot options (2-week Dedicated POC):
- H100 pilot (recommended for strict p95<=100ms validation): 4 x H100 reserved for 2 weeks — estimated trial commit: USD 85,000–95,000 (one-time pilot commit).
- A100 pilot (cost-balanced): 6 x A100 80GB reserved — estimated trial commit: USD 50,000–60,000.
- L40S pilot (cost-light): 8 x L40S reserved — estimated trial commit: USD 30,000–38,000.

What’s included: automated benchmarking with your traces, per-route latency and first-byte metrics, engineering time for tuning quantization/serving config, and a final performance report with recommended production sizing.

Required from Helix to start the POC:
- Signed pilot commitment or purchase order (we can route a short SOW).
- Sample traces and representative payloads (we’ll use these to run the 3-hour baseline).
- SOC2 evidence request: we’ll provide our SOC2 summary; you noted additional evidence would be sent to your security team.

Proposed timeline: pilot kickoff week of Feb 23rd if we get commitment by Feb 18th.

If this looks good I’ll draft the pilot SOW and pricing sheet.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Michael Choi <michael.choi@helixdx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Jessica Lewis <jessica.lewis@helixdx.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & pilot commercial terms — Helix Dedicated POC

Marissa/Aditya — thanks, that all looks reasonable. We’re aligned to run the POC against the stricter p95<=100ms for priority flows.

Action items from Helix:
- We will provide sample traces and representative payloads by Feb 16th (San Francisco team).
- Security will follow up with a request for SOC2 artifacts — please send the SOC2 summary and the auditor contact.
- We are inclined to try the A100 pilot first (cost/perf tradeoff) and if the p95 target is not met we’ll flip to H100 for the production commit.
- We’ll route a purchase order (PO) for the 2-week pilot by Feb 18th if the SOW looks standard.

Can we schedule the 3-hour baseline benchmark for Feb 24th (10:00–13:00 PST)? Please confirm availability and any pre-work we should run on our side.

Thanks,
Michael Choi
Head of Infrastructure | Helix Diagnostics
